thread:
alex.h: Quick status: bringing up Aegis7B from vendor checkpoint. Int8 conversion looks fine, but int4 is showing a ~3% MMLU regression and weird token duplication in long-context summarization.

marie.k: any error logs or repros?

alex.h: Repro steps:
```bash
# quantize
python tools/quantize.py --model ./vendor/aegis7b/model.safetensors --out ./build/aegis7b.int4 --bits 4 --perchannel
# run eval (local CI)
./bench/run_eval.sh --model ./build/aegis7b.int4 --tasks mmlu,bbh --seed 42
```
Failures show up in longctx where generated summaries repeat a token cluster, and backend logs a kvcache index error intermittently: `IndexError: kv_cache index 1024 out of range for seq_len 512` (seen on shards 2 & 3).

ravi.p: hmm. Two things to check: 1) tokenizer mapping (vendor uses NFKD + soft-hyphen/token fallback), 2) rotary/kv indexing assumptions — if token ids shifted by any offset kv_cache slot lookups will mismatch per-head.

alex.h: I diffed the vendor vocab vs our canonical. There's a block of 8 special codepoints (0xAD soft-hyphen, NBSP variants) mapped differently and vendor left a reserved hole at id 32000. When quantizing we pack weights with headwise layout, and a tiny id shift cascades into wrong head offsets for some implementations.

jen.s: can you paste the minimal failing stack?

alex.h: ```py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"runtime/serve.py\", line 421, in _step
    kv_idx = kv_index_for_token(token_id)
IndexError: kv_cache index 1024 out of range for seq_len 512
# followed by inference producing repeated token clusters like: \"the the the\" in summaries
```
kai.t: I hit a similar symptom on another model where rotary_scale computation assumed lexicographic token ordering. Quick mitigation: remap token ids pre-inference to our canonical space, OR apply a head-offset correction when building kvcache indices.

marie.k: do we have a remap script?

alex.h: added a quick mapping script and smoke test: `scripts/convert_vocab.py --from vendor/vocab.json --to redwood/vocab.json --map maps/aegis_map.json` — after remapping, int4 pass rate improves locally. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/2023 (WIP) includes the mapping table and an additional check that token ids are contiguous before packing.

ravi.p: worth noting: the int4 packer assumes `num_heads * head_dim` alignment. If token id reordering causes per-head offsets to point to wrong Kv rows you'll get the exact IndexError. Two safe choices: 1) enforce remapped contiguous ids before pack, 2) fallback to int8 for now.

jen.s: let's not ship int4 until we ensure mapping is in the conversion pipeline. Can we add a CI gate?

alex.h: will add a CI check that runs `scripts/verify_vocab_contiguous.py` during model-convert + a short eval (MMLU smoke). For now rolling back int4 in the hosting pool for Aegis7B and keeping int8 active.

infra-bot: Deploy rollback triggered by @jen.s for model: aegis7b.int4 at 2024-11-03T15:12:03Z :warning:

kai.t: next steps: 1) merge PR with remap + contiguous check, 2) run full int8 vs int4 comparison on 24h bench with remap applied, 3) add token-normalization test (NFKC vs NFKD) to tokenizer unit tests.

marie.k: agreed. I'll own the CI gate. Thanks for the fast triage, alex. :thumbsup:
